summary: The game's front door: a title screen with new game, continue, load, settings, credits and quit; one SceneFlow autoload that owns every transition between title, expedition and battle with a fade and a threaded loading veil; a pause menu on Escape; and a suite that walks the whole round trip through the live bridge.

coordination.notes: game/project.godot takes an append at the END of [autoload] plus the run/main_scene line, per the keep-both-tails rule for parallel lanes. expedition_prototype.gd and battle_prototype.gd each take exactly ONE changed line -- the get_tree().change_scene_to_file call becomes the SceneFlow call that owns that transition -- because P7 owns the former and P6 the latter this round; a conflict there is a keep-both tail on one line. campaign_session.gd is extended, not forked: describe_slot gains the active_location_id a save screen has to show, and continue_newest is split so that continue_slot(slot) is the one load path and continue_newest picks a slot and delegates to it. No second save reader enters the tree. SHIPPED: SceneFlow owns all four transitions and the two prototypes carry one changed line each (the change_scene_to_file call became the SceneFlow call). Escape is handled by SceneFlow rather than by a hook in either prototype, so the pause menu cost those two files nothing beyond that one line. An autoload's name is not a compile-time identifier in a `--script` run -- the whole project already reaches its autoloads through get_node_or_null for that reason -- so the shell does the same and preloads scene_flow.gd only where a static reader is needed. tools/../game/tools/capture_review_scene.gd was extended (a list of scene/output pairs rendered in ONE engine process, and a pair may name several scenes stacked into one frame) under the owner's Godot-courtesy instruction of 2026-09-06, which asks for exactly that batching; card P1 owns that file and this is an additive change to it.
